L11·N1842unmasked layer
This neuron's strongest responses are large **negative** ones on the word that completes a compound geographic/institutional name inside a comma-separated address string (" Canary" in "Canary Islands", " Channel" in "Channel Islands", " Government" in "Government of India", "-street" in "Dorset-street"), while its (much weaker) positive side just fires on continuation sub-tokens of proper-name/listing strings like "Saurashtra-Ver(aval)", "El Dorado Acres Homes", "WAINGANGA EXP".

This appears to be a structural/positional neuron: it fires on the first token of a newly-started sentence or list item (e.g. "There" after a sentence end, "1)", "(P" opening a parenthetical tag, a clause-ending comma) and is strongly *suppressed* on tokens in the very first words of a document right after `<|begin_of_text|>` (e.g. "system", "can" in "You can…").

This neuron fires on highly predictable "filler" continuation pieces that complete an already-established multi-token pattern — subword fragments of compound names (L-Tar**tr**ate, McAd**ams**), and the repeated/complementary components of numeric structures (the `0` in `<0, 1, 0>`, the `-` in `0-10V`, the `89` complementing `10.21%`) or of parallel constructions ("body **half** of human and half of a horse"); it is suppressed on verbs completing modal/ability frames (can't **afford**, allow **yourself**, **Imagine**).

This neuron has no clean semantic theme (its positive range is tiny, −2.3 to 0.7): it fires weakly on assorted mid-sentence content words continuing a description ("opponent", "another", "molt", "learning", "-inations"), while its real signal is strong *negative* activation on function words and abstract head nouns in object/prepositional position ("the", "about", "rule", "concept") — i.e. it is best characterized as a suppression neuron for determiners/prepositions and generic head nouns.
